answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a remotely verified enclave instance: MRENCLAVE commits to its measured code, while a hardware-protected platform key proves the attestation and prevents ordinary VM copying of credentials. Since MRENCLAVE alone is not unique per chip, identity issuance must also enforce the hardware-key policy; creating another valid identity then requires additional trusted silicon, not merely cloning a nebula image across a karst cluster or deploying a raven process.
